newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says new liquid gas ducts to cut costs.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says new liquid gas ducts to cut costs.

text.p: New liquid petroleum gas (LPG) ducts along Mexico's Pacific coasts should boost the nation's exports of the fuel, state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) said in statement.
Pemex said government and company officials announced over the weekend a new duct from Jaltipan, Veracruz state to Salina Cruz, Oaxaca had begun operations.

Another $40 million duct project with Amoco Corp. in the works will run from Hobbs, New Mexico state to Ciudad Juarez, Chihuahua state and is expected to begin operations this month, the statement said.

The new gasducts will lower prices and costs of distribution in Mexico, and the cross-border Hobbs-Ciudad Juarez duct will lower import costs, Pemex director general Adrian Lajous said at an event marking the new gas duct.
Lajous said the duct will strengthen export volumes and returns because of reduced LPG transportation costs.
In addition, he said the new Jalipan-Salina Cruz duct will eliminate Pemex's dependence on the Panama canal, and specifically strengthen Mexico's competitive position with Ecuador and Peru.
The duct has a capacity of 30,000 barrels per day (bpd) and could expand to between 40,000 and 60,000 bpd with additional construction, Lajous said.
The Hobbs-Ciudad Juarez duct will have the capacity to transport 24,000 bpd.
Mexico's LPG market is the world's largest, Lajous said, although the country is looking to substitute the more polluting fuel with electricity and natural gas.
LPG is subsidized by the government, for a total of 5.176 billion pesos in 1996, 72 percent more than 1995 subsidies.
